glossary.term: A boundary within a domain where a particular domain model applies (Learning DDD).
An insulating translation layer that adapts foreign schemas and third-party APIs into clean internal domain models without leaking external concepts.
The entry-point entity of a cluster of domain objects that encapsulates business logic and strictly enforces consistency invariants across all child entities.
A business rule, constraint, or condition that must always remain true and consistent within an aggregate at all times.
A record of an important business event that has occurred in the domain, used to trigger eventual consistency and async processing pipelines.
A reliable messaging pattern where domain events are committed to a local database outbox table within the same transaction as business data mutations before being published to message brokers.
OWASP API Security #1: A vulnerability where an API endpoint fails to verify that the requesting authenticated user owns the targeted object ID.
OWASP API Security #5: A vulnerability where an API endpoint fails to enforce role-based or permission-based access controls on sensitive business actions or administrative routes.
A critical vulnerability where an attacker manipulates a server into fetching unexpected internal or third-party resources, bypassing network firewalls and metadata services.
A TypeScript union of object types sharing a common literal property ('type' or 'status') that enables exhaustive pattern matching and makes invalid states unrepresentable.
A UX performance principle stating that user productivity and engagement increase exponentially when computer-human response latency remains under 400 milliseconds.
A cognitive UX law stating that decision time increases logarithmically with the number and complexity of available choices.
A psychological observation that human working memory can hold approximately 7 (plus or minus 2) discrete chunks of information at one time.
A fundamental software engineering guideline: 'Be conservative in what you do, be liberal in what you accept from others.'
A deterministic, fully isolated test that executes with zero external network or database dependencies, ensuring zero flaky test runs.
A standard unit test structure that divides test execution into three clearly demarcated phases: setup (Arrange), execution (Act), and verification (Assert).
The five criteria for effective unit tests: Fast, Independent, Repeatable, Self-Validating, and Timely.
An umbrella term for any object that replaces a production collaborator during testing (Fakes, Stubs, Mocks, Spies, and Dummies).
A software engineering metric measuring the degree of coupling between two components based on how a change to one necessitates a change to the other.
The degree to which elements within a single module, class, or package work together to achieve a single, well-defined purpose (High Cohesion is preferred).
The degree of mutual interdependence between software modules (Low Coupling is preferred).
A concise document capturing an important architectural decision, including context, alternatives considered, decision rationale, and downstream consequences.
